scope: Explicit offline research evaluation of the published BEIR SciFact archive; not a production search connector.
license: Claims and annotations: CC-BY-4.0; abstract database: ODC-By-1.0, with underlying content rights separate.

rights.retrieval: Explicit no-key download from the fixed university-hosted BEIR archive; check published MD5 and pinned SHA-256.
rights.retention: Keep raw abstracts and indexes locally under ignored .anvesha storage; retain attribution and source hashes.
rights.display: Show local benchmark records for assessment; the public report contains metrics and identifiers, not abstract prose.
rights.redistribution: Redistribute the selected CC-BY-4.0 queries/annotations with attribution and transformation notes. Do not bundle/relicense the abstract corpus or infer article rights from the database licence.
rights.evaluation: Use the published evidence annotations for scientific document retrieval; do not describe them as fresh Anvesha human judgments or a general-web study.
rights.training: No training in this slice. Evaluation queries are reserved from project tuning; any future training has a separate rights/privacy decision.

attribution: SciFact authors David Wadden, Shanchuan Lin, Kyle Lo, Lucy Lu Wang, Madeleine van Zuylen, Arman Cohan and Hannaneh Hajishirzi; BEIR authors Nandan Thakur, Nils Reimers, Andreas Rucklé, Abhishek Srivastava and Iryna Gurevych; S2ORC authors Kyle Lo, Lucy Lu Wang, Mark Neumann, Rodney Kinney and Daniel S. Weld.
limitations: Only English scientific claim-evidence retrieval; no live-web freshness, factual truth, or Google/SearXNG parity claim.
Relevance labels are inherited upstream annotations; unlisted query-document pairs are unjudged, not proven irrelevant.
No raw abstract text is committed to this repository or returned by production APIs by preparing the benchmark.
Selected training claims and all BEIR test claims form development/evaluation splits. Public data can have appeared in model training.
